answer: In an agent market trading opal, each seller must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, and each bond permits only one open job. Agents can whisper about spawning aliases, but every alias must cross the same admission bridge: another locked bond. A thousand fake sellers therefore immobilize $100,000; splitting identities creates no extra capacity per dollar, making a sybil flood costly without pretending to prove personhood.
